candidate.title: Car Wrap Advertising Scam
candidate.summary: Scammers offer people hundreds of dollars a week to drive around with their car wrapped in a major brand's advertising, then send a fake cashier's check that leaves victims owing the bank money after they wire funds to a "vendor."
safetyTips: Never deposit a check from a stranger and wire back or send part of the money via a payment app before the check has fully cleared, which can take weeks
Contact the brand named in the ad directly through its official website to verify whether it actually runs a car wrap advertising program
Be suspicious of any work-from-home or gig offer that pays you upfront and only requires you to forward funds to a third party
Report suspected car wrap scams to BBB Scam Tracker and the FTC
candidate.howItWorks: A victim sees an ad or gets a text claiming a major brand will pay them to wrap their car, truck, or boat in company advertising. After filling out an application, a "boss" contacts them with instructions and mails a cashier's check meant to cover the cost of installing the wrap. The victim is told to deposit the check and use part of it to pay a specific "local vendor" via Venmo or Cash App who will supposedly install the wrap. Because the check initially appears to clear, the victim sends real money to the scammer-controlled vendor before the bank discovers the check is counterfeit, leaving the victim responsible for repaying the full fake amount plus any bank fees.
redFlags: Unsolicited offer to pay hundreds of dollars a week just for driving with an ad wrap on your car
You're sent a check and told to deposit it, then immediately send part of the money elsewhere via Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, or wire transfer
The employer contacts you only through text message and never in person or via a verifiable company channel
You never met the 'vendor' and were told exactly which one to pay
The job requires no interview and pays out before any actual work (driving/advertising) has occurred
realExamples: BBB Scam Tracker reports referencing brands including RedBull, Utz, and Breyers used in fake car wrap job offers
Illinois BBB (Rockford Regional Office) warned in May 2025 that car wrap scams were 'heating up' as scammers target people seeking warm-weather side gigs via text messages and online ads
Victims report depositing a mailed cashier's check, paying a 'local vendor' through Venmo or Cash App, then having their bank flag the check as counterfeit and hold them responsible for the balance

triage.reasoning: This is a fake-check job scam using a specific "wrap your car in advertising" pretext, similar in mechanism to Mystery Shopper Check Scam (fake check, victim wires part to a third party, bank later reverses check) but with a distinct enough hook and category placement to warrant separate listing; however, the truncated BBB source provided contains no actual substantive details supporting the candidate's specific claims (dollar amounts, Venmo/Cash App instructions, etc.), only site navigation boilerplate, so verification is weak.
